issue.label: Weekly issue / pilot 001
issue.title: This week in the Nature Coast
issue.subject: Clear water, greasy breakfasts, and one smarter way to test the move
issue.summary: The newsletter is the push. The site is the destination. This issue surface turns the offline template idea into a live, Vercel-readable product: weekly picks, weather, guide cards, sponsor inventory, and source discipline in one place.
picks: Paddle or snorkel Kings Bay before you make any emotional real-estate decisions.
Three Sisters / Hunter Springs for the postcard version of why people care about Crystal River.
Ozello sunset drive into Peck's Old Port Cove. Not polished. Correctly weird.
Silver Springs glass-bottom boats or paddling if you want old-school Florida without logistics hell.
Start with guided paddles, marina hubs, parks programming, farmers markets, and volunteer/outdoor groups.

cards.title: Three Sisters Springs
cards.body: Start here for the cleanest emotional proof of the Nature Coast: clear spring water, manatee context, and the reason the region has pull.

cards.title: Morning water, flexible afternoon
cards.body: Build the day around heat, wind, and thunderstorm risk. The Weather Pulse turns that into a quick go/no-go layer.

cards.title: Ozello Trail into Peck's
cards.body: Windows down, marsh edge, seafood, sunset. It is not polished. That is the point.

cards.title: Guided paddles and markets
cards.body: The meet-people plan starts with repeated, low-pressure local overlap instead of awkward generic networking.

dayTrips.title: Crystal River / Kings Bay
dayTrips.body: Morning clear-kayak or manatee tour, lunch at The Biscuit Barn or Sadie's, Hunter Springs decompression, sunset at Fort Island.

dayTrips.title: Homosassa / Ozello
dayTrips.body: GoBoat or river tour, MacRae's vibe check, Ozello Trail drive, Peck's Old Port Cove for seafood and marsh-at-the-edge-of-the-world energy.

dayTrips.title: Ocala / Gainesville
dayTrips.body: Silver Springs in the morning, downtown Ocala lunch, Gainesville for Satchel's, Curia, Kanapaha, or a night with actual college-town motion.

places.name: Three Sisters Springs
places.blurb: The postcard. Clear spring water, manatee context, and the emotional reason this region makes sense.

places.name: Hunter Springs Park
places.blurb: Easy access to water without turning the whole day into a logistics project.

places.name: Paddles Outdoor Rentals And Tours
places.blurb: Clear-kayak and paddleboard tours near Pete's Pier. Good first social/outdoor activity.

places.name: Crystal River Kayak Company
places.blurb: Practical rental base for paddling toward Three Sisters and Kings Bay.

places.name: Bird's Underwater
places.blurb: Serious contender for a guided manatee experience, and guided trips are one of the easier newcomer social lanes.

places.name: GETAROUNDBOAT
places.blurb: Best fit for the two-people-cruising-not-hauling-ass idea. Small electric GoBoat style outings.

places.name: MacRae's of Homosassa
places.blurb: Boat-ramp, river-hub, old-Florida personality. Useful for learning the local water scene.

places.name: Ozello Trail
places.blurb: Windows-down marsh-road drive that makes the Gulf edge feel strange in the right way.

places.name: Fort Island Beach
places.blurb: Not Malibu. Still useful: sand, sunset, and salt air without committing to an Atlantic run.

places.name: Peck's Old Port Cove
places.blurb: Go for the drive, seafood, and old-school waterfront feel.

places.name: The Biscuit Barn
places.blurb: High-confidence first greasy breakfast stop.

places.name: Jr's Smashburgers
places.blurb: Smashburger target for the Crystal River/Homosassa side.

places.name: Beans and Greens Coffee House
places.blurb: Local healthy-ish reset near the core area.

places.name: Rainbow Springs State Park
places.blurb: Swimming, tubing, kayaking, and the easiest way to understand the Dunnellon side.

places.name: Silver Springs Glass Bottom Boats
places.blurb: Old-school no-effort water day: sit down, look through glass, see the spring.

places.name: Silver Springs Paddling Adventures
places.blurb: Kayak, canoe, and SUP rentals inside Silver Springs State Park.

places.name: The Canyons Zip Line
places.blurb: The rare inland Florida thing that does not feel flat.

places.name: Satchel's Pizza
places.blurb: Beloved, wacky Gainesville stop. Pizza plus weird art-yard energy.

places.name: Curia On The Drag
places.blurb: Coffee/vegan/artist-compound vibe and a better social surface than another chain cafe.

places.name: Kanapaha Botanical Gardens
places.blurb: Bamboo, gardens, shade, and a civilized reset after highway/boat-ramp scouting.

places.name: Paynes Prairie
places.blurb: Bison/alligator watch, wide-open prairie, and a more cinematic Florida than expected.

places.name: Withlacoochee State Trail
places.blurb: The boring-looking thing that becomes very useful if you live nearby.

places.name: Cedar Key
places.blurb: Small Gulf island town with old docks and end-of-the-road mood.

places.name: Crystal River Preserve
places.blurb: Good for testing whether daily nature access feels like home instead of vacation.

places.name: New Smyrna Beach Jetty
places.blurb: The realistic Central Florida surf mission when Gulf life is not enough.

places.name: MDR Jet Ski Rental
places.blurb: Closest named Crystal River jet ski rental found. Call first and ask about two-person scenic riding.
